Save a results table to Word, LaTeX, HTML, or CSV

Source: R/export.R
cr_save.Rd

The format follows the file extension:

  • .docx: Word table (also the best route into Google Docs: upload the file to Drive and open it with Google Docs, or copy the table from Word).

  • .tex: booktabs LaTeX float for Overleaf; \input{} it from your document.

  • .html: standalone page; open it in a browser, select the table, and paste into Google Docs or an email.

  • .csv: the formatted cells, for anything else.

Usage

cr_save(x, path, caption = NULL, label = NULL, landscape = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A clean_results, cr_table, cr_text, cr_ground_truth, or ggplot object. Pass a cr_table to control the table style, e.g. cr_save(cr_table(res, style = "se"), "t2.tex").

path

Output file path.

caption

Table caption (LaTeX and Word/HTML).

label

LaTeX \label{} key, e.g. "tab:main".

landscape

Word only: put the table on a landscape page.

...

Passed to cr_flextable() (Word/HTML) or cr_latex() (LaTeX).

Value

path, invisibly.

Details

Report text from cr_report() saves to .tex (for \input{} in Overleaf), .md, .html (open in a browser and paste into Google Docs to keep italics), or .txt. A cr_ground_truth() saves to .json, .md, or .csv.

A ggplot (e.g. from cr_plot_means()) saves as a figure: .pdf (vector, fonts embedded), .svg, .eps, .png, or .tiff (600 dpi). Pass width = "1col", "1.5col" (default), "2col", or a width in mm, and optionally height in mm.
